{"rationale":"Evidence from the race (iteration 0 development trials): the robot finished 3 of 20 oval trials and none of the s-bend or slalom trials. Almost every run ended off track, with max_error near the 0.06 m limit, and line loss occurred about once per run on the s-bend and slalom. Progress on those tracks was only 0.12 to 0.17, so the robot left the line early in the first sharp bends. Steering oscillation was highest on the oval (0.31), which suggests the proportional response is too aggressive or under-damped at the current speed. Three changes address this:

1. Sensor coverage. The original span was +/-0.04 m with 12 mm sensors. On sharp bends the tape leaves the array, which causes line loss. I widened the span to +/-0.06 m (the largest useful spacing, since 0.08 is the limit) and enlarged the sensors to 16 mm so the 25 mm tape stays under at least one sensor at larger offsets. Sensors sit 0.06 m ahead of the axle to read the line before the wheels reach it.

2. Speed. base_speed drops from 1.5 to 1.2. The robot has less time to correct at speed, and the off-track limit is only 0.06 m. Some completion time is traded away, but a completed run on any track is worth 500 points, so completion matters more.

3. Damping and inertia. kd rises from 0.3 to 0.8 to damp the oscillation, and kp rises modestly from 2.5 to 3.5 so the robot corrects faster on the wider sensor span. A small ki of 0.1 helps hold the line on sustained bends. Body length drops to 0.14 m and mass to 0.7 kg, which reduces yaw inertia so the robot turns more readily.

Sensor weights stay [-2,-1,0,1,2] (positive signal steers left, matching the sensor order right to left). line_loss stays last_direction so the robot searches toward the side it last saw the line.
